findings.title: Adjective locked to the boy
findings.claim: The closing adjective makes purity a quality of the bestowed boy.
findings.mechanism: Its indefinite accusative masculine singular agreement and supplied attachment place it under ghulaman, not under the giving act or the beneficiary.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the gift resolve into the character of the one who is given.
findings.containment: The adjective remains a local quality of the concrete boy; it is not recast as a separate action or as a quality of Maryam or the gift event.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus morphology and attachment support directly establish the adjectival relation.

findings.title: Speech lands on purity
findings.claim: The answer closes on the announced boy's purity rather than stopping at the act of giving.
findings.mechanism: The final position of zakiyya follows purpose, beneficiary, and object, so the spoken gift is completed by the quality attached to its object.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the announcement settle on what kind of child is being given.
findings.containment: Final placement adds closure to the gift phrase; it does not by itself assert a separate event or a conclusion beyond the supplied quality.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-word analysis and final-position support directly establish the landing effect.

findings.title: Growth and purity held together
findings.claim: The boy is marked by purity that also carries a pressure toward growth in goodness.
findings.mechanism: The supplied z-k-w root-family evidence holds increase and purification together while the local adjective keeps both pressures attached to ghulaman.
findings.reader_payoff: Purity becomes more than absence of stain: it can be heard as goodness taking shape in a developing life.
findings.containment: The root pressure colors the local adjective without turning the boy into an abstract process or displacing the ordinary concrete quality.

epistemic.reason: Trusted support explicitly preserves the growth-purity pairing while narrowing broader root-family pressures to the local adjective.

findings.title: Bounded purity thread
findings.claim: The final purity adjective can be heard against the supplied purity vocabulary around Surah 19 and the contrastive contexts in Surah 18.
findings.mechanism: The cited contexts give the focus adjective a lexical field of purity, soundness, and replacement while its local agreement still makes the boy the carrier of the quality.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing word connects this child's announced quality with a wider supplied vocabulary without losing the immediate scene.
findings.containment: This is a bounded lexical contact from the supplied references, not a surah-wide thesis and not a claim that the neighboring contexts determine the focus reading.

epistemic.reason: Trusted support supplies the cited purity contexts, while the focus morphology limits the contact to a bounded lexical coloration.

findings.title: Stable purity quality
findings.claim: Purity is presented as a stable characteristic of the announced child, not as a single deed performed in the moment.
findings.mechanism: The supplied local form is a qualitative adjective, and its rare adjectival realization gives the final word a characteristic rather than eventive function.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader receives the child as bearing a quality, not merely as having completed an act of purification.
findings.containment: The characteristic quality does not imply an unlimited theological or biographical claim; it describes the supplied adjectival presentation.

epistemic.reason: Trusted morphology and contextual profile establish the qualitative form and its local effect.

findings.title: Annunciation dialogue chain

findings.mechanism: Qala turns the preceding encounter into a reported answer, and the cited 19:8, 19:9, and 19:21 parallels connect the boy formula to dialogue rather than silent narration.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the child announcement as a reply that belongs to the surrounding birth-announcement exchange.
findings.containment: The supplied parallels illuminate the speech pattern; they do not add another event or make the focus a summary of those scenes.

epistemic.reason: Trusted speech and dialogue-chain supports supply the lexical contact and its boundary.

findings.title: Completed direct-speech frame

findings.mechanism: The perfect speech verb governs the following words through the final adjective, so the identity and gift beats remain inside one direct-speech frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes an answer being spoken rather than a narrator paraphrasing what happened.
findings.containment: The frame establishes who is speaking and how the words are delivered; it does not decide the truth of every proposition inside the speech.

epistemic.reason: Trusted attachment and focus-word evidence directly establish the quoted complement.

findings.title: Delayed speaker disclosure

epistemic.reason: Trusted perfect-form and speech-frame evidence directly supplies the implicit-subject and later self-definition relation.

findings.title: Restricted declaration
findings.claim: The reply answers the threat-frame of 19:18 with a declaration that restricts the figure to messenger-status.
findings.mechanism: Innama asserts and excludes before the role noun appears, turning Maryam's conditional challenge into controlled self-identification.

findings.containment: The restriction qualifies the figure's role in this reply; it does not remove the later mission or claim that every aspect of the encounter is exhausted by one label.

epistemic.reason: Trusted boundary, restriction, and cadence supports directly establish the response relation.

findings.title: Fused restriction parse
findings.claim: The fused restriction particle leaves the following nominal identity clause free while still asserting limitation.

findings.containment: This is a syntactic qualification of the restriction; it does not weaken the semantic boundary or turn the clause into an ungoverned fragment.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC parse and attachment support directly supplies the construction and its semantic effect.

findings.title: Identity before purpose

epistemic.reason: Trusted scope and attachment supports establish the clause order and its discourse effect.

epistemic.reason: Trusted cadence support establishes the audible and positional effect, while its interpretive coloring remains bounded.

findings.title: Explicit nominal self

findings.containment: The explicit self identifies the speaker's role; the construct and restriction still keep that role relational and bounded.

epistemic.reason: Trusted nominal-attachment evidence directly establishes the subject-predicate relation.

findings.title: Envoy bound to Rabb

findings.title: Bestowal names recipient and object
findings.claim: The purpose clause names both Maryam as beneficiary and the boy as the direct object of the intended gift.

findings.reader_payoff: The gift has a grammatically visible destination and content rather than remaining an unspecified promise.
findings.containment: The object reading rests on the supplied governing construction, not on accusative case alone; the beneficiary remains distinct from the object.

epistemic.reason: Trusted purpose and attachment supports directly establish the recipient-object structure.

findings.title: Free child-gift field
findings.claim: Ahaba places the announced boy in a supplied field of free divine gift rather than exchange or ordinary consequence.
findings.mechanism: The root's bestowal sense and the cited child-gift scenes at 19:5, 3:38, 14:39, and 21:72 make the object a granted life within the lexical field of gift.
findings.reader_payoff: The boy is heard as bestowed without a compensating transaction, seizure, or merely ordinary result.

epistemic.reason: Trusted root-family and intertext support establish free-bestowal pressure while the local purpose clause limits its application.

findings.title: Variant agency pressure
findings.claim: The supplied variant makes divine agency more grammatically explicit while the canonical wording lets the messenger speak in the first person as the mediated giver.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive mediated and source-level agency together without having to choose one wording as the winner.
findings.containment: The variant is a bounded contrast and does not replace the canonical surface, rank the readings, or detach either agency from the named Rabb.

epistemic.reason: Trusted variant support explicitly preserves the agency contrast while narrowing it to the canonical and accepted forms supplied.

findings.title: Maryam as beneficiary
findings.claim: Maryam is named as the beneficiary before the boy is named as the gift's object.

findings.reader_payoff: The recipient is foregrounded before the content of the gift comes into view.
findings.containment: The beneficiary relation is distinct from the direct-object relation and does not assert ownership or a different grammatical role for Maryam.

epistemic.reason: Trusted beneficiary attachment and focus-word analysis directly establish the recipient relation.

findings.title: Pronoun relation reversal
findings.claim: The purpose-for-you sequence turns the immediate address from the fear-from-you posture of 19:18 toward a gift-for-you relation.
findings.mechanism: The repeated lām pattern links li-ahaba with laki, and the supplied boundary evidence contrasts laki with Maryam's earlier min-ka relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The same encounter shifts from protecting herself against the figure to hearing what is intended for her.
findings.containment: The relation changes within the supplied discourse boundary; it does not erase the fear-frame or claim that the two prepositional phrases have identical syntax.

epistemic.reason: Trusted repeated-lām and boundary supports supply the local reversal and keep it tied to the immediate scene.

findings.title: Same suffix shifts relation
findings.claim: The same second feminine singular suffix keeps Maryam as the addressee while changing her grammatical relation from sender-related dependent to beneficiary.
findings.mechanism: The suffix appears in rabbiki under the construct's genitive relation and in laki under the beneficiary prepositional relation, with different governors shaping its role.
findings.reader_payoff: The addressee remains constant while the scene moves from whose Lord is named to what is intended for her.
findings.containment: The repeated suffix establishes continuity of address, not sameness of syntax or an additional claim about Maryam's status.

epistemic.reason: Trusted suffix and attachment evidence directly establishes the repeated form and changed relation.

findings.title: Birth-announcement formula
findings.claim: Ghulaman participates in the supplied boy-announcement formula that links this scene with the nearby birth announcements.
findings.mechanism: The concrete noun appears as the announced object in the cited 19:7, 19:8, 19:20, 15:53, and 51:28 formulations, while zakiyya gives this occurrence its distinctive qualifier.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the object as an announced boy within a repeated speech pattern, not as an abstract offspring label.
findings.containment: The supplied formula is lexical and dialogic background; it does not import the neighboring scenes or determine the focus adjective by itself.

epistemic.reason: Trusted birth-announcement support supplies the repeated formula and the local noun remains concretely attached to this gift.

findings.title: Male youth qualified by purity
findings.claim: The gift is a concrete male child or youth whose developmental vitality is directed toward purity.
findings.mechanism: The gh-l-m noun supplies the boy or young-male image, and the following z-k-w adjective qualifies that life with disciplined moral growth rather than leaving it as generic offspring.
findings.reader_payoff: The announced gift appears as a developing human life with a marked direction of goodness.
findings.containment: The noun remains a boy or youth and the adjective remains its supplied quality; no exact age, abstract offspring sense, or later biography is added.

epistemic.reason: Trusted noun, root-family, and adjective supports preserve the developmental image while the local form bounds it.

findings.title: Gift object completed by adjective
findings.claim: The boy is both the object of the bestowal and the noun whose quality completes the gift phrase.
findings.mechanism: The supplied governing and attachment evidence assigns ghulaman as ahaba's direct object and makes zakiyya dependent on that noun.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the gift object arrive together with the quality that defines it.
findings.containment: The object relation comes from the full construction rather than accusative marking alone, and the adjective does not become a separate object or action.

epistemic.reason: Trusted attachment and bestowal-frame supports directly establish both relations.

findings.title: Concrete nominal scene-word
findings.claim: Ghulaman presents a concrete boy or male-youth object in the announcement rather than a broad verbal root event.
findings.mechanism: The supplied QAC morphology identifies an indefinite accusative noun, and the contextual profile keeps the local word in a nominal announcement role.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene remains visibly about someone being announced as a gift, not about an abstract process called forth by the root.
findings.containment: The root-family developmental background can color the noun, but the local nominal form controls what is actually being announced.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC and nominal-scene support directly establish the concrete noun profile.

findings.mechanism: The messenger carrier at rasūlu meets the Rabb carrier and the free-bestowal carrier across the identity-to-purpose sequence, so the proximate speaker delivers rather than independently originates the gift.
